topStories.headline: Bayview Gets Its First Blueprint for Cleaner Air — and a Chance to Shape It Tuesday
topStories.dek: The Bay Area Air Quality Management District released a long-awaited draft pollution reduction plan for Bayview–Hunters Point on September 14; residents can weigh in at a public open house this Tuesday evening.
topStories.body:
After more than two years of community steering-committee meetings, the Bay Area Air Quality Management District released a Public Review Draft of the Bayview Hunters Point/Southeast San Francisco Community Emissions Reduction Plan on September 14, 2026. The 238-page document is available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Tagalog, Vietnamese, Samoan, and Tongan, and is now open for public comment. It represents the neighborhood's first formal, community-driven blueprint for tackling industrial pollution, freeway diesel, and legacy contamination from the Hunters Point Naval Shipyard.

The plan was developed under California's Assembly Bill 617, a state law that directs resources to communities bearing disproportionate pollution burdens. Bayview Hunters Point/Southeast San Francisco was designated the fourth AB 617 community in the Bay Area, joining West Oakland, Richmond–North Richmond–San Pablo, and East Oakland. The goal is to identify and accelerate actions — selected by residents themselves — that go beyond existing state and regional programs to deliver direct reductions in local air pollution and health risk.

Residents have an immediate opportunity to shape the final document. The Air District is holding a public Open House on Tuesday, September 22, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at the Southeast Community Center, Alex Pitcher Pavilion, 1550 Evans Street. Interpretation services are available upon request. The Marie Harrison Community Foundation and Bayview Hunters Point Community Advocates have served as co-equal partners throughout the planning process, and the community steering committee has held more than 20 meetings since the effort launched in early 2024.

The stakes are significant. The neighborhood has one of the highest mortality rates and lowest life expectancy figures in all of San Francisco, with major pollution sources including industrial facilities, waste-management sites, and two freeways — I-280 and US-101 — that bracket the community. The final plan is expected to establish enforceable reduction targets, a reduction strategy, an implementation schedule, and an enforcement plan carried out by the Air District, the California Air Resources Board, and community partners.

topStories.headline: India Basin Waterfront Park Throws a Block Party This Weekend — and Closes the Street to Try Something New
topStories.dek: The park hosts a free Family Day Block Party on Saturday, September 19, alongside a weekend-long test of slower, pedestrian-friendlier conditions on Innes Avenue and Hunters Point Boulevard.
topStories.body:
India Basin Waterfront Park is hosting a free Family Day Block Party on Saturday, September 19, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. along Hunters Point Boulevard between Innes and Hudson avenues. The event will feature live music and DJs, dance performances, live painting, a free photo booth, community art, local vendors, nonprofit tables, and BBQ from Surfside Liquor, according to the park's official website.

The celebration is paired with a weekend-long trial of temporary street changes on Innes Avenue and Hunters Point Boulevard, in place from Friday, September 18 through Sunday, September 20. The test is designed to make the streets around the park slower and safer for pedestrians and cyclists — infrastructure advocates have long argued such changes are needed so that Bayview–Hunters Point residents can fully benefit from their new waterfront park.

The 10-acre India Basin Waterfront Park is a $200 million environmental-justice investment that opened its southern section at 900 Innes Avenue in October 2024. Built on a remediated brownfield, the park gives Bayview–Hunters Point residents waterfront access for the first time in generations and includes two new piers, a floating dock, a food pavilion, and a makers' shop. Renovation of the adjacent India Basin Shoreline Park — the third and final phase of the project — is ongoing. A separate grand community celebration is scheduled for October 19.

topStories.headline: Visitacion Valley's Brand-New Night Market Returns to Leland Avenue Next Friday
topStories.dek: The inaugural Visitacion Valley Night Market series — launched on the last Friday of each month this summer — holds its second and final 2026 installment on September 25, with food, music, dancing, and local vendors filling a closed Leland Avenue.
topStories.body:
Visitacion Valley's first-ever neighborhood night market returns to Leland Avenue on Friday, September 25, from 4 to 8:30 p.m., with the street closing between Bayshore Boulevard and Peabody Street from noon to 10 p.m. The free event is the second installment of an inaugural monthly series that launched on August 28. The SFMTA posted the event details and transit reroutes on September 16, noting that the 56 Rutland bus will detour around the closure.

The market features food vendors, local shopping, live music, street dancing, family-friendly activities, and tables from community organizations. The series is presented with support from the Civic Joy Fund and the Southside Community Development Corporation. All ages are welcome.

The market is the latest sign of renewed investment along Leland Avenue, Visitacion Valley's de facto main street. SF Heritage has noted that the corridor has faced pressure from demolitions of historic storefronts while also gaining new energy through the Visitacion Valley Greenway parks and the SF Crosstown Trail. The monthly night market adds a recurring focal point to a street that community groups have long worked to revitalize.

moreNews.headline: Black-Owned Bookstore and Café Planned for Third Street in Bayview
moreNews.body: Vanessa Lee, owner of Smoke Soul Kitchen on Third Street, filed a permit application in July 2026 to open Chapter 3 — a Black-owned bookstore and café — at 4512 3rd Street in Bayview–Hunters Point, Mission Local reported on July 29. Lee told the outlet she was inspired by Marcus Books, the legendary Black-owned Fillmore bookstore that relocated to Oakland in 2014. The planned space would host author readings and live performances, shift to a wine bar in the evenings, and run a used-book exchange program focused on titles by Black authors. No opening date has been announced.

restaurants.name: Old Skool Cafe
restaurants.description: A 1920s speakeasy-themed supper club run by at-risk and formerly incarcerated youth, serving global soul food and live jazz every night it's open.

restaurants.name: Gumbo Social
restaurants.description: Chef Dontaye Ball's Bayview brick-and-mortar serves acclaimed build-your-own gumbo, po'boys, and smoked meats; recently reopened after a six-week retooling.

restaurants.name: All Good Pizza
restaurants.description: A beloved outdoor pizza spot in a sun-drenched garden, serving thin-crust Neapolitan pies made with organic, locally sourced ingredients; open Tuesday–Saturday.

restaurants.name: Gratta Wines
restaurants.type: Urban winery, wine bar & Italian market
restaurants.description: San Francisco's last mainland urban winery, founded in 2006 by Barbara Gratta, offering Dry Creek Valley wines, Italian small bites, and a specialty market on Third Street.

restaurants.name: Cafe Alma
restaurants.description: A welcoming community café on Third Street in the Bayview, serving coffee, food, and hosting local events and creative workshops.

restaurants.name: Beep's Burgers
restaurants.description: An Ocean Avenue institution since 1962, serving juicy burgers, curly fries, legendary garlic fries, and milkshakes at a retro drive-in counter open daily until 2 a.m.

restaurants.name: Ocean Ale House
restaurants.description: Ingleside's social anchor at 1314 Ocean Avenue, with rotating craft beers on tap, pub food, a small live-music stage, open mic nights, and a welcoming all-ages atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Megan's Table
restaurants.description: A family-run café on Ocean Avenue serving Thai and Cambodian dishes including cha kroeung, papaya salad, pad see ew, and Tom Kha soup in a warm, plant-filled setting.

restaurants.name: Pho Golden
restaurants.description: A casual Excelsior Vietnamese restaurant well-regarded for its pho and dishes featuring grilled pork.

restaurants.name: Calabria Brothers
restaurants.description: An Excelsior Italian deli counter known for oversized, generously filled sandwiches made to order.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Familiar
restaurants.description: An Excelsior neighborhood staple serving Salvadoran and Mexican fare with praised entrees at family-friendly prices.

restaurants.name: Los Planes de Renderos
restaurants.description: A popular Excelsior Salvadoran spot focused on pupusas and traditional Central American comfort food.

restaurants.name: Don Chuy's
restaurants.description: A beloved Excelsior corner store recognized for its outstanding carnitas burrito.

restaurants.name: 7 Mile House
restaurants.description: A Visitacion Valley landmark at Bayshore Boulevard and Geneva Avenue, one of San Francisco's oldest continuously operating bars, still serving drinks on the same corner for generations.

restaurants.name: Pakwan
restaurants.description: A reliable Ocean Avenue spot for tandoori chicken, chicken achar, and hearty Pakistani and Indian dishes served in generous portions.

shops.name: SCRAP (Scroungers' Center for Reusable Art Parts)
shops.description: San Francisco's beloved 50-year-old nonprofit creative reuse depot, now in a permanent new home at 141 Industrial Street — five times the size of its former warehouse — selling donated materials at low cost to artists, teachers, and makers.

shops.name: Flora Grubb Gardens
shops.description: A beloved open-air destination garden center at 1634 Jerrold Avenue in the Bayview, widely regarded as one of the finest plant shops in the Bay Area.

shops.name: Meizzei Hardware
shops.description: A legacy hardware store on the Third Street corridor that has served the Bayview community for decades.

shops.name: Ocean Subs
shops.description: An Excelsior lunch staple praised for its Original Sub on toasted Dutch crunch, stacked with Italian meats and a tangy herb vinaigrette.

artEntertainment.name: Ruth Williams Opera House (Bayview Opera House)
artEntertainment.type: Historic performing arts and cultural center
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest extant theater and Landmark #8, the Ruth Williams Opera House is the cultural anchor of Bayview–Hunters Point, hosting concerts, theater, Stoop Sessions, community events, and youth arts programs.

artEntertainment.name: Jerry Garcia Amphitheater
artEntertainment.description: A free outdoor amphitheater named for the late Grateful Dead frontman, set within McLaren Park and hosting summer concerts and community performances.
artEntertainment.address: 100 John F. Shelley Dr, McLaren Park

artEntertainment.name: Quesada Gardens
artEntertainment.description: A vibrant community-built gathering space at Quesada Avenue and Newhall Street, transformed since 2006 with greenery, colorful murals, and tiled stairs.

gymsRecreation.name: Excelsior Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: A boutique Excelsior studio on the third floor of the US Bank Building on Mission Street, offering classical 90-minute Hatha yoga classes blended with science, pranayama, and meditation.

gymsRecreation.name: John McLaren Park
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's second-largest park, spanning Visitacion Valley and the Excelsior with over seven miles of trails, a swimming pool, tennis and basketball courts, a golf course, soccer fields, playgrounds, and the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater.

gymsRecreation.name: Crocker Amazon Playground
gymsRecreation.description: A large southern San Francisco park featuring a skate park, lighted soccer fields, basketball and tennis courts, children's play areas, and baseball and softball fields currently in a renovation planning process.

gymsRecreation.name: India Basin Shoreline Park
gymsRecreation.description: A newly developed waterfront park on the Bayview shore offering San Francisco Bay views, restored native habitat, and public shoreline access.
